title: FO4 Papyrus function index: every function, script function and event handler declared by the shipped Fallout 4 base scripts

provenance.note: the shipped Fallout 4 base .psc sources, read read-only. 7854 files, 11.5 MB.

run papyrus_index.py/1 on 2026-10-03. Extraction is textual: comments and string bodies blanked, then declarations matched. NO COMPILER WAS RUN, so nothing here is compile-verified. The strongest claim available from source alone is that a declaration exists.

provenance.source: not read, and therefore absent from every count
provenance.note: Source/User/ (66 .psc, Vortex-managed mod content), the DLC0*.zip script archives (extracting writes outside the project, which policy section 8 forbids), and the Creation Kit install, which is not present on this machine. Every usage count is therefore a LOWER BOUND.

prose: Generated, not written. Every entry is a declaration read out of the shipped Fallout 4 base scripts; none of it is recalled from documentation, which is how the hand-written negative table in ai_context/papyrus_syntax_rules.md came to be wrong on its first two rows. Entries are keyed by ScriptName.FunctionName because Papyrus namespaces on the declaring script and because a bare-name existence test is unsafe: SendEvent does not exist as an FO4 engine function, and it occurs three times in the FO4 base scripts as a locally defined script function at CA_TopicInfoScript.psc:36. The per-function detail a caller needs to branch on -- arity, parameter names and types, the native and hidden keywords, observed call counts -- lives in the top-level attributes and usage maps rather than on the entry, because schema.json declares no field for any of them and that file belongs to another owner. entries is a projection of attributes written from the same record in one pass, so the two cannot disagree, and tools/papyrus_index_gate.py verifies that they do not.

scan.hidden_measurement_note: MEASURED NEGATIVE, and it is a Skyrim-contamination trap: the word `hidden` occurs 1,194 times across these scripts and NOT ONCE on a function or event declaration. In Skyrim and SKSE, `Function Foo() native hidden` is idiomatic; in the FO4 base scripts `hidden` is a SCRIPT flag only, alongside native, debugonly and betaonly. A modder or a language model importing the Skyrim idiom gets a compile error here that reads like a missing function.

case_collisions_note: Declarations that differ only in casing, which a case-insensitive language reads as one. Keys in `entries` and `attributes` are folded so the file loads in consumers with case-insensitive keys -- PowerShell's ConvertFrom-Json refuses a JSON object whose keys differ only in case, and policy section 5 names ConvertFrom-Json as the verification. MEASURED: this list is EMPTY for all 7,854 files. That is a result, not an untested path. An earlier draft that ignored State blocks reported 262 collisions here; every one was a false positive, because TrapTripwire.psc declaring OnActivate at line 76 and again at 125 is one handler per state (Auto state Active, then state Inactive), and Papyrus allows the same event name once in each state.
usage_attribution: Per-declaration usage is NOT reported per declaration, and cannot be. Papyrus resolves a call against the receiver's STATIC TYPE, so a text scan that sees `x.Stop()` cannot say whether it bound to Quest.Stop, Scene.Stop, EffectShader.Stop, VisualEffect.Stop or TestMovement.Stop. Every usage figure here is therefore keyed by NAME in `name_level`, counted once, and carries `declared_by` so a reader can see how many declarations share it. An earlier draft of this tool summed the family total across all declarers and so reported Stop as 7,125 calls where 1,425 call sites exist; the five-fold inflation was an artefact of the aggregation, not a measurement.

crosscheck_note: papyrus_syntax_rules.md section 1 against this run. Four verdicts, because 'the name is absent' and 'the name exists but not in the role the claim was about' are different facts. CONTRADICTED means the markdown is wrong and the exact contradicting declaration is carried in engine_declarations. PRESENT_BUT_NOT_THE_THING means the name is declared by an ordinary script rather than by the engine. The engine/script split is decided by the native flag on the DECLARING SCRIPT, not by a hand-written list of engine types: a Papyrus function may be declared Native only if its script is also flagged Native (papyrus_syntax_rules.md section 4), so engine-provided base-type scripts are Native and quest scripts are not. SendEvent is the instructive case -- it is absent as an engine function and occurs three times as a quest script's own helper at CA_TopicInfoScript.psc:36, so a bare-name existence test would have reported FO4 as having it. Start, Stop, GetLength and GetSize are receiver-scoped: they exist, but as members of specific engine types (Quest, Scene, EffectShader, VisualEffect, ObjectReference, FormList) and not of ScriptObject, so the practical advice in the markdown survives while its blanket wording does not.

schema_fit.why: Closest declared kind in ai_context/spec/schema.json: 'A callable in a host scripting API, whether or not it exists.' Its entry_required set (name, exists, signature, container, provenance) maps onto this data without inventing anything.
schema_fit.finding_owed_to_owner: NO declared kind fits a function index. api_function declares no field for arity, parameter types, the native or hidden keywords, or a usage count, and this repository does not own schema.json, so no kind was invented. Those fields are carried in the top-level `attributes` and `usage_summary` maps, which spec_lint does not police because it checks entry fields only. The correct fix is a declared kind in schema.json; until then the split between `entries` and `attributes` is a workaround, and it should be read as one.
